summary: Santiago Peak lookout, Orange County, CA: lookout by 1912, tower built 1913 (or 1914), 35-ft tower 1951; cab gone by 1988, tower stands on an AT&T relay building in a communications site.

facts.design: Original two-level ground-mounted peak-roof structure (1913); 75-ft X-brace steel tower by 1930, lowered to 20 ft in the late 1940s; 1951 35-ft H-brace steel tower with a cab (13x13 ft per FFLOS, 10-ft per FFLA-SDRC)
facts.status_note: Cab removed by 1988; the tower and catwalk still stand on top of an AT&T relay building (FFLOS). FFLA-SDRC says the remaining structure is surrounded by communications facilities.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Cleveland National Forest (Trabuco Ranger District)

staffing.status: staffed by lookout men in 1912 and 1913; still in use in 1929; Forest Service stopped using it in the late 1970s or early 1980s

access.note: Active communications site on Cleveland National Forest land; FFLOS calls it the busiest communications site in the United States. No public visiting rule appears in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Part of an active communications facility; do not climb the relay building or tower. No public visit information in the sources read.

events.note: Forest Supervisor appointed a lookout in June 1912; Eugene Davis named lookout in July 1912 (newspaper items quoted on the weebly page)
FFLOS gives 1913 for the first tower; FFLA-SDRC gives 1914. Newspapers show a lookout and cabin on the peak already in 1912.
A September 1929 item credits the Santiago Peak lookout with helping keep three lightning fires small
By October 1930 a modern 75-foot tower stood on the peak (newspaper item quoted on weebly). FFLOS says the 1913 structure was replaced in the 1930s.
FFLA-SDRC says the CCC removed the original tower in 1935. The sources do not say which structure that was.
A 35-foot tower replaced the lookout; FFLOS gives a 13x13 ft cab and FFLA-SDRC a 10-ft cab
AT&T built a telephone relay building on the lookout site; a tower and cab were added to its roof
AT&T removed the cab by 1988; the tower and catwalk still stand on the building
Registered February 17, 2009 as US 518, CA 4; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.why: 22.9 m (75 ft) is the 1930s X-brace tower. FFLOS says it was lowered to 20 ft in the late 1940s, and both FFLOS and FFLA-SDRC describe the 1951 replacement as 35 ft. The height of the structure on the relay building is not given.

corrections.current: The tower still stands, but its cab is gone (FFLA).
corrections.proposed: Cab removed by 1988; the tower and catwalk still stand on top of an AT&T relay building (FFLOS).
corrections.why: The cab removal and the catwalk are in the FFLOS detail page. FFLA-SDRC does not say the cab is gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS gives 1913 for the first tower and FFLA-SDRC gives 1914. Newspaper items from June 1912 describe a lookout with a small cabin on the peak. The record keeps 1913 from the FFLOS 'Built' field and notes the 1912 lookout and FFLA's 1914.
FFLOS gives a 13 by 13 ft cab for the 1951 tower and FFLA-SDRC gives a 10-ft cab. Both are kept and the story notes the difference.
FFLA-SDRC says the CCC removed the original tower in 1935, but a 1930 newspaper item already refers to a modern 75-foot tower. Which structure the CCC removed is left unresolved.
The FFLOS detail page we read says the tower and catwalk still stand. The brief lists FFLOS as 'gone', which the detail page does not support. Treated as standing.

notes_for_editor: Read: the FFLOS detail page (firetower.org), the FFLA-SDRC page, the weebly page (newspaper excerpts 1912-1930, read through targeted grep windows; the page is long and only part of it was seen), Wikipedia (excerpt), and the firelookout.org California list (the Santiago line was not readable; the grep window was cut). The brief's 'fflos=gone' is not supported by the FFLOS detail page, which says the tower and catwalk still stand; the firelookout.org list line should be checked. The 22.9 m height is corrected to the 35-ft 1951 tower. Staffing names come from 1912-1913 newspaper excerpts quoted on the weebly page; the originals were not checked. The CCC 1935 removal is unclear against the 1930 75-ft tower reference. Access is set to restricted from the communications-site description; no public-access rule was found. The 1964 relay-building tower may not be the 1951 tower; the sources do not say. No photos were added. The FFLOS page says the 1930s replacement was lowered in the late 1940s; the exact year is not given.
